Evaluate module-trait relationships in a WGCNA network

rna_wgcna_module_trait.Rd

Evaluates associations between module eigengenes and experimental groups using correlation analysis. The function uses module eigengenes obtained during WGCNA network construction to identify modules associated with a binary experimental condition.

Experimental groups are encoded as a binary trait, with the reference group represented by 0 and the comparison group by 1. Pearson correlation coefficients, corresponding p-values, and Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values are calculated for each module.

Results include a module-trait association table and correlation matrix. An optional heatmap can be generated to visualize the direction and magnitude of module-trait relationships.

Usage

rna_wgcna_module_trait(
  project,
  group = NULL,
  reference = NULL,
  plot = TRUE,
  save = TRUE
)

Arguments

project

An rna_project object containing a previously constructed WGCNA network generated by rna_wgcna.

group

Optional character vector specifying the two experimental groups to compare. Both groups must be represented among the samples included in the original network. If NULL, groups are automatically identified when exactly two non-missing groups are available. Defaults to NULL.

reference

Optional character string specifying the reference group. The reference group is encoded as 0, whereas the other selected group is encoded as 1. If NULL, the first selected group is used. Defaults to NULL.

plot

Logical. If TRUE, generates a heatmap displaying module-trait correlation coefficients, with colors representing their direction and magnitude. Defaults to TRUE.

save

Logical. If TRUE, attaches the analysis result to the project under analyses$wgcna_module_trait and invisibly returns the updated project. Otherwise, invisibly returns an object of class wgcna_module_trait_result. Defaults to TRUE.

Value

If save = TRUE, invisibly returns the updated rna_project object containing the module-trait analysis result.

If save = FALSE, invisibly returns an object of class wgcna_module_trait_result, containing:

  • module_trait_results: a data frame containing module identifiers, colors, selected groups, correlation coefficients, p-values, and FDR-adjusted p-values.

  • correlation: a matrix of module-trait correlation coefficients.

  • pvalues: a matrix of corresponding statistical p-values.

  • parameters: a list containing selected groups, correlation settings, and sample counts.

  • timestamp: date and time of analysis.

Input requirements

The function requires a previously constructed WGCNA network containing module eigengenes. Sample metadata must contain the columns Sample and Group, with unique sample identifiers matching the row names of the module eigengene matrix.

Metadata are automatically aligned to the eigengene matrix, and samples outside the selected groups are excluded. Samples with missing group assignments or incomplete eigengene values are also excluded.

Both selected groups must contain at least one complete observation, with at least three complete samples available overall.

Analysis

Module-trait relationships are evaluated using Pearson correlations between each module eigengene and the binary experimental trait. For binary traits, this is mathematically equivalent to a point-biserial correlation.

Positive correlations indicate higher eigengene values in the comparison group, whereas negative correlations indicate higher values in the reference group.

Statistical significance is estimated using the Student approximation implemented in corPvalueStudent. P-values are adjusted across modules using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure to control the false discovery rate (FDR).

Results are ranked by adjusted p-values, and the selected contrast is recorded in the resulting object.

Interpretation

Correlation magnitude reflects the strength of the association between module eigengenes and the experimental condition. Statistical significance should be interpreted together with correlation magnitude, sample size, and adjusted p-values.

Module-trait associations identify modules whose expression patterns are associated with the selected condition, but do not establish causal relationships or demonstrate direct regulation of module genes.

Scope and limitations

The function evaluates one binary contrast at a time and does not adjust for additional covariates, confounding factors, repeated measurements, or other sources of sample dependence.

The analysis uses module eigengenes calculated during network construction and does not identify differential co-expression or changes in network topology between experimental groups. Designs involving relevant covariates or complex sampling structures may require complementary regression or mixed-effects models.

References

Langfelder P, Horvath S. (2008). WGCNA: an R package for weighted correlation network analysis. BMC Bioinformatics, 9, 559. doi:10.1186/1471-2105-9-559
